- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for the next 5–7 days.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5), especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast by 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (0.00) over last 5–7 days, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 7–10 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >75 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
- For horizon >15 days, model often underestimates downward trend; add 0.5–2% to forecast if sentiment is negative or neutral over last 7 days.
- If sentiment spikes to 0.33 or higher, model tends to lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply upward bias only if sentiment persists.
